France / PLANNING GUIDE

France Travel Planning Guide

Choose a starting city, a season and a manageable route for your France break.

By Travelber Editorial · Updated 19 October 2026

IN THIS GUIDE

The short versionChoose a starting cityMatch the plan to your stayChoose a seasonKeep the route practicalBefore you bookOfficial sources
← France overview

The short version

Explore France through riverfront cities, Mediterranean ports, regional food traditions and historic neighbourhoods.

First break2–3 nightsSuggested approachOne baseStart comparingParis

Choose a starting city

  • Paris: Paris combines Seine-side landmarks with major art collections and distinctive neighbourhoods.
  • Lyon: Lyon brings together Renaissance streets, silk-working heritage and traditional bouchon restaurants.
  • Marseille: Marseille centres its Mediterranean maritime identity on a working harbour and hillside neighbourhoods.
  • Nice: Nice pairs a Mediterranean seafront promenade with the narrow streets and markets of its old town.
  • Bordeaux: Bordeaux combines grand stone architecture along the Garonne with a strong wine culture.

Compare all ten cities

Match the plan to your stay

For two nights, keep one city as your base. With three or four nights, add a second neighbourhood or a carefully checked day trip. For a longer stay, compare actual journey times before adding another base; the city collection is not a suggested rail circuit.

Choose a season

Festival programmes vary by season and year; check dates before planning around a particular event. Keep a weather alternative for outdoor sightseeing.

Keep the route practical

Check the exact departure and arrival stations: SNCF Connect can suggest alternative stations around your chosen city. Allow time for transfers across Paris when your journey changes stations.

Read the transport guide

Before you book

  • Confirm your arrival station or airport and the last connection to your stay.
  • Choose one priority experience per day.
  • Check entry times and cancellation terms with the venue.
  • Keep an indoor alternative and compare total accommodation costs.

Official planning sources

  • France tourism
  • France journey planning

Editorial planning suggestions, not a personal trip report. Check opening dates, ticket conditions and live journeys before booking.
